title: Running speed unresolved — posterior ambiguous, audio/video disagree
summary: Do not treat speed as confirmed. Bayesian speed posterior (scale-invariant prior, 15/18 peaks explained) p_map=0.152 at 680.6 rpm, with competing modes 318.4 rpm p=0.361, 387.7 rpm p=0.292, 506.6 rpm p=0.194 — all <0.8 threshold. A 2-pole/50 Hz what-if was also ambiguous: p_map=0.208, modes 246.3 rpm p=0.375, 318.4 rpm p=0.257, 387.7 rpm p=0.208. display_rpm=null, so no independent check. text:
## Assessment — optimisation withheld pending a valid speed capture

**Running speed is unresolved.** The Bayesian posterior is multimodal: 680.6 rpm at p=0.152, with competing modes at 318.4 rpm (p=0.361), 387.7 rpm (p=0.292) and 506.6 rpm (p=0.194). This is well below the p≥0.8 confidence threshold. Audio blade-pass tracking instead indicates 48.104 Hz / 2886 rpm. A 2-pole, 50 Hz alternative was also tested and remained ambiguous (p_map=0.208). No display rpm was available as an independent check.

**No ISO 20816 severity can be reported.** The amplitude scale is uncalibrated (`scale_calibrated=false`, overall zone null). The apparent 275.9–334.2 mm/s RMS channel values are therefore relative only and must not be treated as Zone D measurements.

**Structural modes identified:** 2.298 ±0.230 Hz (damping unknown), plus FDD modes at 2.068 Hz and 2.528 Hz (damping unknown), 8.963 Hz (ζ=3.1%) and 11.491 Hz (ζ=5.0%). Resonance is the highest evaluable fault hypothesis at p=0.413, but its range is wide (0.225–0.685) and there are no Campbell criticals, so resonance is possible—not confirmed.

**Cavitation and looseness are not supported:** cavitation p=0.048 with index 0.281, HF energy fraction 0.0198 and kurtosis 1.209; looseness p=0.0043 with no qualifying shaft harmonics.

**Imbalance, misalignment, vane-pass, bearing and electrical faults are not evaluable** from this capture; all measured 1×/2×/3× orders are 0.0 mm/s.

### Required recapture before optimisation
Provide a tachometer/encoder-synchronised, calibrated triaxial accelerometer capture, with shaft phase, axial and both-sides-of-coupling measurements, plus the nameplate rpm, poles, power and impeller vane count. Once shaft speed and any variable-speed range are confirmed, critical-speed margins, duty, specific energy and NPSH can be assessed safely.

**No setpoint is proposed:** proposing one now would rely on an unresolved speed, uncalibrated amplitudes and an empty Campbell diagram.
